title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Executive Overview / Business Environment (qualitative retention and record new card acquisitions statements)
key_points: The filing states that net card fees increased 17% year over year 'as new card acquisitions reached record levels in 2022 and Card Member retention remained high.'
The filing attributes billed business growth to 'our continued ability to acquire, engage and retain high-spending, premium Card Members.'
No numeric card member retention rate is disclosed in this passage or elsewhere in the retrieved filing content; retention is described only qualitatively as 'high'.

The filing attributes results to 'increased generational relevance with Millennial and Gen Z customers, record new card acquisitions, deeper relationships with customers and expanded merchant acceptance.'
No numeric net card additions figure (gross acquisitions minus attrition) is provided in this passage.

title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — Note 24: Reportable Operating Segments (segment realignment and recast)
key_points: Effective for the third quarter of 2022, American Express realigned its reportable operating segments to reflect organizational changes announced during the second quarter of 2022, and prior periods were recast to conform to the new segments.
Effective for the first quarter of 2022, the company updated the methodology used to allocate certain revenues, with prior period amounts recast to conform to current period presentation.
The four reportable operating segments are U.S. Consumer Services (USCS), Commercial Services (CS), International Card Services (ICS) and Global Merchant and Network Services (GMNS).
Because of the recasts, segment-level 2021 and 2020 figures are presented on a recast basis rather than as originally reported.
raw_excerpt: Effective for the third quarter of 2022, we realigned our reportable segments to reflect organizational changes announced during the second quarter of 2022. Prior periods have been recast to conform to the new reportable segments.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Business Environment / Executive Overview (p45)
key_points: 管理层称 2022 年网络消费达到创纪录水平，信用指标仍低于疫情前水平。
管理层将业绩归因于产品创新、技术、人员与品牌投入带来「increased generational relevance with Millennial and Gen Z customers」、创纪录的新卡获客、更深客户关系与商户受理扩张。
Billed business 占网络流量 86%，同比 +23%（FX 调整 +25%），管理层表述为体现「continued ability to acquire, engage and retain high-spending, premium Card Members」。
U.S. Consumer billed business 同比 +24%，管理层归因于 premium U.S. consumer Card Members 的消费趋势持续强劲。
净卡费同比 +17%，管理层归因于 2022 年新卡获客创纪录且 Card Member retention remained high，并称体现对 premium value propositions 的投入。
服务费及其他收入同比 +36%，部分由更高的旅行相关收入驱动；净利息收入同比 +28%，主要由 Card Member loans 增长驱动。
Card Member loans 同比 +22%，管理层称增长「majority of growth coming from existing Card Members」，由 billed business 强劲增长驱动，并指出该增长在年末因「lapped the steep phase of recovery」而开始放缓。
2022 年净利润 $7.5B（每股 $9.85），2021 年 $8.1B（每股 $10.02）；下降反映信用准备金计提与 Amex Ventures 投资净亏损（上年为准备金释放与净收益）。
raw_excerpt: Our investments in product innovation, technology, people and our brand has led to increased generational relevance with Millennial and Gen Z customers, record new card acquisitions, deeper relationships with customers and expanded merchant acceptance. … Billed business, which represented 86 percent of our total network volumes and is the most significant driver of our financial results, increased 23 percent year-over-year (25 percent on an FX-adjusted basis), demonstrating our continued ability to acquire, engage and retain high-spending, premium Card Members. U.S. Consumer billed business grew by 24 percent year-over-year, reflecting continued strength in spending trends from our premium U.S. consumer Card Members. … Net card fees increased 17 percent year over-year, as new card acquisitions reached record levels in 2022 and Card Member retention remained high, demonstrating the impact of investments we have made in our premium value propositions. … Card Member loans increased 22 percent year-over-year, with the majority of growth coming from existing Card Members and was driven by ongoing strong growth in billed business, which began to moderate towards the end of the year as we lapped the steep phase of recovery.
